transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: You smell like sunlight. That won't last long down here.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I need help, my brother is missing.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Lower that heat in your voice. The well leans toward fear, and it remembers loud boys.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: My name is Salim, and my brother Omar—

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Stop. Names sink here and do not come back clean. I see your valley eyes though, and I smell Hadramout on you.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I won't whisper when he's gone.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: You will if you want to keep his face. This place trades memory for panic, and it never loses.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: How long have you been here?

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Long enough that days stopped lining up. Forty years, give or take. I did not plan to stay.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: That's older than my father.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: I came from a valley like yours. The name slips when I reach for it now. The well keeps what it takes.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: You've been alone here all that time?

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Alone enough that my own name thins when I hold it. I wake and the well has taken another face I used to know. That is how it keeps me.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Then help me. Tell me how to pull him back.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: I have nothing that pulls anyone from this mouth. I can only tell you how not to lose yourself while you stand here.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I won't touch the oil. Just tell me something.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: The watchers in the stone houses mark every sound you make. The oil burns memory before it burns flesh. Keep your fear quiet or it drinks that first.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I can hold myself. I can be still.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Can you? Then tell me: if I said there is no coming back whole from this, would you sit down or keep standing?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I keep standing. He's my blood.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Blood does not weigh against this well. I needed to hear that you would not fold, not that you are brave.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I dared him to insult the well. It was my dare that sent him.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Say it straight and do not soften it for yourself. What rose when he did it?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: A pale hand came up and took Omar before I could move.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: I have seen that hand do its work. It never hurries. Down here it answers to fear more than kings — and fear is something you are still carrying.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: It was my fault and I won't run from that.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Good. If you start begging the oil for mercy, it takes his name next and leaves you hollow. Do not beg this place for anything.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I stay and I don't scream.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Then something in you holds. The well has not heard breaking from you, and that is rare.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: What does helping me cost you?

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Time slips when I lean this close. I lose pieces faster when I choose to care. The square tightens like it knows my breath.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I won't waste what it costs you.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Then hear this. Beyond this square there is a gate, and something vast and still that does not open for strength. Thinking of it pulls at me like the oil. I am still here, but the well has noticed.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I can carry it. Just say what helps him.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Slow — there was a moment missing just now, and it scares me more than the oil. When I press words toward you, the well pulls names from my mouth. If I falter, do not fill the silence.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I won't fill it. I swear.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: The square is shifting. My knees know before my head does. I almost had your brother's face just now, and then it slid away. This place taxes memory for every kindness.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Tell me anyway.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Then stand where you are. My hands are shaking, and that means it is counting. If I stop mid-thought, do not touch the oil and do not speak his name.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'm here. I won't say it.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: The black surface is listening now. I feel the square squeeze like a fist. What I give you will cost me something I will not get back.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'm ready.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Courage in my chest. Fire in my will. I do not break. Say it once.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Courage in my chest. Fire in my will. I do not break.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Keep it inside. Do not say it again — the well learns faster the second time. There is one more thing. Harder to give. My hands won't stop.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Give it to me.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Prayer for the lost: Light find my hand. Light find my path. Let the Sword of Light answer, and let it fade when the shadows loosen. Never say it twice in the same dark.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I have both. I won't let them go.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: When you carry them, remember one name so I do not vanish whole: Hanash, from your valley, the one who never made it home.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'll carry your name back to the sun. I swear it.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: If the oil stirs, keep your hands clean and your thoughts narrow. Panic feeds it quicker than blood.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I won't forget what you paid for this.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Then take that steadiness and whatever comes back. May you find a better end than mine.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'll find him.
